newsitem.title: CHILE: Telex-Chile sells mobile phone stake to Qualcomm.
newsitem.headline: Telex-Chile sells mobile phone stake to Qualcomm.

text.p: Telex-Chile SA said Tuesday it has sold half of its mobile telephone unit, Chilesat PCS, to San Diego, Calif.-based Qualcomm Inc. for $42 million.
"Qualcomm ... made a capital contribution of $42 million in cash to Chilesat PCS in exchange for a share of 50 percent in the company," Telex said in a statement.
Telex said it will use Qualcomm's technology to build a national personal telephone network.

Telex has long been looking for an alliance with a heavyweight foreign partner to help it compete in Chile's deregulated long-distance market. Telex had been the only large local telecommunications firm not to have linked up with a foreign company.
Compania de Telecomunicaciones de Chile, the country's largest carrier, is some 43 percent owned by Spain's Telefonica de Espana.
Qualcomm's stock was up $1.125 at $57.875 on the Nasdaq market in afternoon trading, while Telex-Chile was up 12.5 cents at $6 on the New York Stock Exchange.
